questions.q: A sponsor wants to start the complaint project by connecting an LLM to the QMS this week. Under the six-step method, what comes first?
options: Interviewing the people who handle complaints
Choosing the model and running it on last month's complaints to show quick value
Writing the prompt
Removing the QMS
questions.why: The method starts by interviewing every role; the LLM only comes at step six.

questions.q: Mapping shows the same complaint typed into the service tool, the CRM and the QMS, and nobody reads the CRM copy. What should happen?
options: Keep all three copies, since more copies mean less risk
Agree with the owner and QA to drop the CRM step via a procedure change
Delete the CRM copy quietly
Automate all three entries with AI so nobody has to re-type anything again
questions.why: Remove redundant steps first, but through a controlled procedure change agreed with QA.

questions.q: When validating the complaint data, which check matters most for later evidence gathering?
options: The font used in emails
How long each complaint text is
Whether lot numbers are filled and exist in MES
Whether complaint texts are long enough for the LLM to summarise them well
questions.why: Missing or unknown lot numbers break the link to production records and weaken every draft.

questions.q: Validating the system finds that investigators can edit closed complaint records. What should you do?
options: Ignore it, the LLM will compensate
Build the LLM first and fix it later
Note it as a known limitation and connect the LLM anyway, since drafts are reviewed
Have QA fix the role permissions before connecting the LLM
questions.why: System gaps must be fixed first; an LLM cannot make up for weak controls.

questions.q: Which complaint step is the best fit for an LLM?
options: Signing the reportability decision
Submitting the report to the FDA
Drafting the QMS entry from a service email for a person to check
Closing low risk complaints automatically when the draft says no investigation is needed
questions.why: Drafting from unstructured text fits; decisions, submissions and closure stay with qualified people.

questions.q: Why does the order of the six steps matter?
options: An LLM applied to duplicate steps and bad data automates the waste
Regulators require exactly six steps
Regulators require exactly six steps for any software change in a quality system
The LLM needs the steps for training
questions.why: Cleaning the process and data first means the LLM lands where it adds value.
